The ferry timetable, explained

The winter timetable has always been a compromise between the tides and the school run, and this year the operator has finally published the reasoning behind it, which turns out to be more interesting than the timetable itself. Every departure is tied to a window of water deep enough for the loaded boat, and the windows move by about fifty minutes a day, so a fixed clock-face timetable was never possible.

What the operator did instead was to fix the first and last crossings to the school day and let everything in between drift with the tide, publishing a fortnight at a time on paper at both slipways. Regular passengers say they stopped reading it years ago and simply ask the skipper, who has been known to wait a minute for a running child and never for a running adult.
